- _Quercus oerstediana_ R.Br.ter | _**Quercus garryana**_ is an [oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak "Oak") tree species found most commonly in the [Pacific Northwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Northwest "Pacific Northwest"), with a range stretching from southern [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") to southwestern [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-6) It is commonly known as the **Garry oak, Oregon white oak** or **Oregon oak**. It is named for [Nicholas Garry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Garry "Nicholas Garry"), deputy governor of the [Hudson's Bay Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson's_Bay_Company "Hudson's Bay Company"). ## Description _Quercus garryana_ is typically of medium height, growing slowly to around 80 feet (24 metres) and occasionally as high as 100ft (30m), or in [shrub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrub "Shrub") form to 10 to 15ft (3.0 to 4.6m) tall. The trunks grow to 3ft (0.91m) thick, exceptionally 5ft (2m). The [bark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bark_(botany) "Bark (botany)") is gray and fissured.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:022-7) It has the characteristic oval profile of other [oaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak "Oak") when solitary, but is also known to grow in groves close enough together that crowns may form a canopy. The [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaves "Leaves") are [deciduous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deciduous "Deciduous"), 2–6in (5.1–15cm) long and 1–3 in broad, with 3–7 deep lobes on each side, darker green on top and finely haired below.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:022-7) The [flowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower "Flower") are [catkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catkin "Catkin"). The [fruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruit "Fruit") a small [acorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acorn "Acorn")[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-9)3⁄4–1in (19–25mm) long, rarely 1+1⁄2 in, and 1⁄2–3⁄4in (13–19mm) broad, with shallow, scaly cups. Its fall color is unspectacular, with many trees turning plain brown. The Oregon white oak is commonly found in the [Willamette Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willamette_Valley "Willamette Valley") hosting the mistletoe _[Phoradendron flavescens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoradendron_flavescens "Phoradendron flavescens")_.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:022-7) It is also commonly found hosting [galls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galls "Galls") created by [wasps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gall_wasp "Gall wasp") in the family Cynipidae. ' [Oak apples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_apples "Oak apples")', green or yellow ball of up to 5cm in size, are the most spectacular.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-10) They are attached to the undersides of leaves. One common species responsible for these galls is _Cynips maculipennis_. Another common predator is the oak twig gall wasp ( _Bassettia ligni_), which causes dead twigs and small branches, especially near the tips of branches. Its effects are cyclic, with successive years producing highly variable amounts of oak twig die-back.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-11) Other species create other galls on stems and leaves. Shapes vary from spheres to mushroom-shaped to pencil-shaped. Individual specimens can grow to around 500 years in age, such as those on [Sauvie Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauvie_Island "Sauvie Island") near [Portland, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon").[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:022-7) The genus name _Quercus_ comes from Latin meaning "oak tree."[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-12) The Garry Oak ( _Quercus garryana_), also called Oregon white oak, ranges from British Columbia to California. [\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-13) The latin scientific name, _Quercus garryana_, was bestowed by Botanist David Douglas in the early 1800's to honor his friend, Nicholas Garry, an officer in the Hudson Bay Trading Company. [\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-14) The Garry oak ( _Quercus garryana_) is one of 20 native oak species found on the Pacific Coast of Northern America, but the only native oak found in western Washington or British Columbia. As the fruit matures, the [involucre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Involucre "Involucre") hardens and becomes a shallow receptacle that contains an acorn. - [![Oregon white oak leaves](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Quercus_garryana.jpg/500px-Quercus_garryana.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Quercus_garryana.jpg "Oregon white oak leaves") Oregon white oak leaves ## Taxonomy ### Taxonomic history [David Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Douglas_(botanist) "David Douglas (botanist)") was the first non-native person to record the species. _Quercus garryana_ is named after [Nicholas Garry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Garry "Nicholas Garry"), who was deputy governor of the [Hudson's Bay Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson's_Bay_Company "Hudson's Bay Company") from 1822 to 1835 and a supporter of Douglas.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:022-7) ### Varieties There are three [varieties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(botany) "Variety (botany)") of Garry oak: - _Quercus garryana_ var. _garryana_ – tree to 65 (100) ft. British Columbia south along the Cascades to the California Coast Ranges. - _Quercus garryana_ var. _breweri_ – shrub to 15ft; leaves velvety underneath. Siskiyou Mountains. - _Quercus garryana_ var. _semota_ – shrub to 15ft; leaves not velvety underneath. Sierra Nevada.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-USDA-16) ## Distribution and habitat It grows from sea level to an elevation of 690ft (210m) in the northern part of its range, and from 980 to 5,900ft (300 to 1,800m) in the south of the range in California.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-GOERT-17) In [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia"), the Garry oak grows on the [Gulf Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Islands "Gulf Islands") and southeastern [Vancouver Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver_Island "Vancouver Island"), from west of [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_British_Columbia "Victoria, British Columbia") along the east side of the island up to the [Campbell River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campbell_River_(Vancouver_Island) "Campbell River (Vancouver Island)") area. There are also small populations along the [Fraser River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraser_River "Fraser River") on the British Columbia mainland.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-GOERT-17) The northernmost population of Garry oak can be found just below 50°N on [Savary Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savary_Island "Savary Island"), in the northern stretches of the [Strait of Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strait_of_Georgia "Strait of Georgia").[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Savary-18) The Garry oak is the only oak native to British Columbia, and one of only two oaks (along with the [bur oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bur_oak "Bur oak")) native to western Canada.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-19) In [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)"), the tree grows on the west side of the [Cascade Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cascade_Range "Cascade Range"), particularly in the [Puget Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puget_Sound "Puget Sound") lowlands, the northeastern [Olympic Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Peninsula "Olympic Peninsula"), [Whidbey Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whidbey_Island "Whidbey Island"), the [Chehalis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chehalis_River_(Washington) "Chehalis River (Washington)") river valley, and the [San Juan Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Juan_Islands "San Juan Islands"). It also grows in the foothills of the southeastern Cascades and along the [Columbia River Gorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_River_Gorge "Columbia River Gorge").[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Burke-20)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Franklin-21) In [Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon "Oregon"), the tree grows on the west side of the Cascade Range, primarily in the [Willamette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willamette_River "Willamette River"), [Umpqua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umpqua_River "Umpqua River") and [Rogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue_River_(Oregon) "Rogue River (Oregon)") river valleys, and along the [Columbia River Gorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_River_Gorge "Columbia River Gorge"), as well as in canyons adjacent to the gorge.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Burke-20)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Franklin-21) In [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), the _garryana_ variety grows in the foothills of the [Siskiyou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siskiyou_Mountains "Siskiyou Mountains") and [Klamath Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klamath_Mountains "Klamath Mountains"), the [Coast Ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Coast_Ranges "California Coast Ranges") of Northern California, and of the west slope of the Cascades. The _semota_ variety grows in the [Sierra Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Nevada_(U.S.) "Sierra Nevada (U.S.)") and Coast Ranges as far south as [Los Angeles County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County,_California "Los Angeles County, California").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-USDA-16) ## Ecology It is a [drought-tolerant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drought-tolerant "Drought-tolerant") tree. Older specimens are often affected by [heart rot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_rot "Heart rot").[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:022-7) The acorns are consumed by wildlife and livestock.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Audubon-8) David Douglas recorded that bears consumed them.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-22) The Garry oak is the obligate host plant of the butterfly _[Erynnis propertius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erynnis_propertius "Erynnis propertius")_ in the northern third of its range _._[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-23) In British Columbia, the Garry oak can be infested by three nonnative insects: the jumping gall wasp _[Neuroterus saltatorius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroterus_saltatorius "Neuroterus saltatorius")_, the oak leaf [phylloxeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylloxeridae "Phylloxeridae"), and the [spongy moth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spongy_moth "Spongy moth").[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-GOERT-17) While the invasive plant disease commonly called [sudden oak death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudden_oak_death "Sudden oak death") attacks other Pacific Coast native oaks, it has not yet been found on the Oregon white oak. Most oak hosts of this disease are in the red oak group, while Oregon white oak is in the white oak group.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-24) ### _Quercus garryana_ woodlands Oregon white oak is the only native oak species in British Columbia, Washington, and northern Oregon. In these areas, oak woodlands are seral, or early- [successional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_succession "Ecological succession"); they depend on disturbance to avoid being overtaken by [Douglas-fir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas-fir "Douglas-fir") ( _Pseudotsuga menziesii_). The disturbance allowing oak to persist in an area that would otherwise succeed to coniferous forest was primarily fire. Natural wildfires are relatively common in the drier portions of the Pacific Northwest where Oregon white oak is found, but fire suppression has made such events much less common. In addition, tribal histories, soil surveys, and early settlers' records indicate that deliberate burning was widely practiced by the indigenous people of these areas. Fire perpetuated the [grasslands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grassland "Grassland") that produced food sources such as [camas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camassia "Camassia"), [chocolate lily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocolate_lily "Chocolate lily"), [bracken fern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bracken "Bracken"), and oak; and that provided grazing and easy hunting for deer and elk. Mature Oregon white oaks are fire-resistant, and so would not be severely harmed by grass fires of low intensity. Such fires prevented Douglas-fir and most other conifer seedlings from becoming established, allowing bunch grass prairie and oak woodland to persist. Fire also kept oak woodlands on drier soils free of a shrub understory. Wetter oak woodlands historically had a substantial shrub understory, primarily [snowberry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphoricarpos "Symphoricarpos").[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Dunn_and_Ewing-25) [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Gallrazorback.jpg/500px-Gallrazorback.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gallrazorback.jpg) Gall on Oregon white oak, Sonoma County Oregon white oak woodlands in British Columbia and Washington are critical habitats for a number of species - Banded cord-moss _Entosthodon fascicularis_ - Apple moss _Bartramia stricta_ - (liverwort) _Riccia ciliata_ - Golden Paintbrush _[Castilleja levisecta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castilleja_levisecta "Castilleja levisecta")_ [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a1/Oregon_oak_grove.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Oregon_oak_grove.jpg) An Oregon white oak grove _Quercus garryana_ woodlands create a landscape mosaic of grassland, savanna, woodland, and closed-canopy forest. This mosaic of varied habitats, in turn, allows many more species to live in this area than would be possible in coniferous forest alone. Parks Canada states that Garry oak woodlands support more species of plants than any other terrestrial ecosystem in British Columbia.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-28) It grows in a variety of soil types, for instance, rocky outcrops, glacial gravelly outwash, deep grassland soils, and seasonally flooded riparian areas.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Dunn_and_Ewing-25)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Lea-26) The [Donation Land Claim Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donation_Land_Claim_Act "Donation Land Claim Act") of 1850 encouraged settlement of Washington and Oregon by the United States and marked the beginning of the end of regular burning by native peoples of the area.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Dunn_and_Ewing-25):Perdue The arrival of Europeans also reduced the number of natural fires that took place in Oregon white oak habitat. With fire suppression and conversion to agriculture, oak woodlands and bunch grass prairies were invaded by Douglas-fir, Oregon ash ( _[Fraxinus latifolia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraxinus_latifolia "Fraxinus latifolia")_), and imported pasture grasses. Oaks were logged to clear land for pasture, and for firewood and fence posts. Livestock grazing trampled and consumed oak seedlings. By the 1990s, more than half the Oregon white oak woodland habitat in the South Puget Sound area of Washington was gone.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Dunn_and_Ewing-25) On Vancouver Island, more than 90% was gone,[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Lea-26) and on Whidbey Island up to 99% of native understory Oregon white oak habitat is gone.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-29) Remaining Oregon white oak woodlands are threatened by urbanization, conversion to Douglas-fir woodland, and invasion by shrubs, both native and nonnative (Scotch broom _[Cytisus scoparius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytisus_scoparius "Cytisus scoparius")_, sweetbriar rose _[Rosa eglanteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosa_eglanteria "Rosa eglanteria")_, snowberry _[Symphoricarpos albus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphoricarpos_albus "Symphoricarpos albus")_, Indian groves in wetter areas that historically had closed canopies of large trees are becoming crowded with young oaks that grow thin and spindly, due to lack of fires that would clear out seedlings.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Dunn_and_Ewing-25) _[Chionodes petalumensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chionodes_petalumensis "Chionodes petalumensis")_ and [valley oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_lobata "Quercus lobata") ( _Q. lobata_).[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-host-31) ## Conservation Oregon white oaks and their ecosystems are the focus of conservation efforts, including communities such as [Tacoma, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tacoma,_Washington "Tacoma, Washington"), where an Oak Tree Park has been established; [Oak Bay, British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Bay,_British_Columbia "Oak Bay, British Columbia"), which is named after the tree; and [Corvallis, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corvallis,_Oregon "Corvallis, Oregon"), which has protected the oak savannah remnants around [Bald Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bald_Hill_(Oregon) "Bald Hill (Oregon)").[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-32) [Oak Harbor, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Harbor,_Washington "Oak Harbor, Washington"), named after the tree[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-33) and home to Smith Park that contains a dense grove of mature Garry Oak trees, formed the Oak Harbor Garry Oak Society to pursue conservation of the city's namesake tree.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-34)[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-35)[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-36) In [Southwest Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwest_Washington "Southwest Washington"), significant acreages of Oregon white oaks are preserved in the Scatter Creek Wildlife Area, in sites such as the [Scatter Creek Unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scatter_Creek_Unit "Scatter Creek Unit"), which contain some of the few remaining areas of south Puget Sound prairie.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-37) In Oak Bay, British Columbia, a fine of up to $10,000 may be issued for each Garry oak tree cut or damaged.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-38) ## Uses The mildly sweet (but perhaps unpalatable) acorns are edible, ideally after [leaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parboiling "Parboiling").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Audubon-8)[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:0-39) The bitterness of the toxic [tannic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tannic_acid "Tannic acid") would likely prevent anyone from eating enough to become ill.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:0-39) [Native Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas") ate the acorns raw and roasted, also using them to make a kind of flour.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:022-7) The hardwood is hard and heavily [ring-porous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wood#Structure "Wood"). It has distinctive [growth rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wood#Growth_rings "Wood") and prominent [rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medullary_ray_(botany) "Medullary ray (botany)"). Heartwood can be a deep chocolate brown color and sapwood will vary from golden brown to nearly white. This makes it particularly attractive to woodworkers; however, it can be difficult to use in woodworking without experiencing warping and cracking.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-40) Although it was popularly used around the turn of the 20th century,[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:022-7) historically the tree has not been regarded as having significant commercial value and is frequently destroyed as land is cleared for development. The wood is suitable for making fence posts. With similar qualities to those of other [white oaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_oaks "White oaks"), the wood has been used experimentally in Oregon for creating [casks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aging_barrel "Aging barrel") in which to age wine.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-41) In Washington, it has been used for aging [single malt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_malt_whisky "Single malt whisky") [whiskey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whiskey "Whiskey") since the 2010s.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-42)[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-43) Oregon white oak barrels are said to give the whiskey "burnt sugar notes, marshmallow sweetness, and a light floral character that showcases the best of the Garry oak".[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-44) When used as firewood, Oregon white oak produces 28million British thermal units per cord (2.3MWh/m3) burned.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-FIREWOOD-45) ## Notes ### Explanatory footnotes 1.
